reasoning_traces.think:
The CLV history is anchored in Neon Postgres, where `odds` table stores timestamped per-book prices. CLOSE snapshots are tagged via `markClosingSnapshots` in settle path, ensuring last pre-kickoff odds are captured. Per-pick CLV columns (`clvCloseLine`, `clvValue`, etc.) are populated at settle time, enabling post-hoc analysis. The CLV decomposition model uses OLS regression to separate information coefficient (IC), liquidity coefficient (LC), and residual error term (epsilon). This structure allows for robust inference of betting performance against closing lines. Failure modes include silent data loss during snapshot writing (e.g., 2026-08-22 to mid-Sept) and mislabeling of residuals as 'sharp money', which violates the honesty rule enforced by `sharpSplitSourced`. The system's cadence is governed by a daily `refresh-odds` cron job at 10:00 UTC, limiting cost while maintaining in-season coverage.
